distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer clinical disease leaf for the full acute cholecystitis spectrum. Calculous, acalculous, emphysematous, gangrenous, perforated, pregnancy-associated, elderly, diabetic, immunocompromised, postoperative, and high-surgical-risk presentations remain risk, context, source-control, event, or future subtype axes rather than disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking may consume RUQ or epigastric pain, Murphy sign, fever or inflammatory labs, cholestatic/hepatocellular labs, and ultrasound/CT/MR imaging evidence. Operative findings, histopathology, culture species or susceptibility, final paper diagnosis, treatment response, and follow-up outcomes remain confirmatory or non-ranking unless a separate post-workup mode explicitly consumes them.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Cystic duct obstruction or gallbladder stasis
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Gallstone, sludge, cystic-duct edema, gallbladder neck impaction, dysmotility, critical illness, ischemia, or prolonged fasting obstructs gallbladder emptying and traps bile.
Obstructed or poorly emptying gallbladder accumulates bile and mucus, raising intraluminal pressure and stretching visceral afferents.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Chemical mucosal injury from concentrated bile
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Concentrated bile, lysolecithin, bile salts, and mucosal edema irritate the gallbladder wall and amplify sterile inflammation even before overt infection.
Stasis and wall injury permit enteric bacterial proliferation or secondary infection, driving neutrophilic inflammation, pus, and sepsis risk.
Inflamed gallbladder serosa irritates adjacent peritoneum and hepatic bed, producing focal tenderness, Murphy sign, pericholecystic fluid, and fat stranding.
Persistent pressure, thrombosis, vascular disease, diabetes, or critical illness compromises gallbladder-wall perfusion and can progress to necrosis.
Local gallbladder inflammation, bacterial products, and complications drive fever, leukocytosis, CRP elevation, tachycardia, hypotension, and organ dysfunction.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Perforation, abscess, or bile peritonitis cascade
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Gangrene or uncontrolled inflammation breaches the gallbladder wall, causing contained pericholecystic abscess, hepatic/subcapsular abscess, free perforation, or bile peritonitis.
Drainage or cholecystectomy decompresses the gallbladder, removes the septic/inflammatory focus, and allows inflammatory and hazard axes to decline.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Gallstones or sludge are the commonest obstructive trigger for acute cholecystitis.
A nonmobile stone at the neck or cystic duct directly blocks gallbladder drainage.
Blocked emptying causes bile/mucus retention and gallbladder distension.
Stagnant concentrated bile injures the mucosa and recruits inflammation.
Stasis and mucosal injury support secondary bacterial growth.
Persistent distension can impair mural perfusion and cause gangrenous change.
Mucosal and mural inflammation extends to serosa and adjacent peritoneum.
Suppurative infection increases local edema, fluid, and fat stranding.
Bacterial products and cytokines drive fever, leukocytosis, CRP, and sepsis physiology.
Necrotic gallbladder wall is prone to perforation and abscess formation.
Effective drainage or cholecystectomy creates the resolution vector.
Drainage or gallbladder removal resolves the obstructed infected reservoir.
Source control lowers bacterial burden in the gallbladder focus.
Source control and drainage reduce ongoing leakage or abscess progression.
Distension and obstructive context are the clinical expression of cystic duct blockage.
Intraluminal pressure produces distended gallbladder on imaging.
Prolonged obstruction can form hydropic gallbladder.
Visceral distension causes steady upper abdominal pain.
Gallbladder pain classically localizes to the right upper quadrant.
Early or atypical gallbladder pain can be epigastric.
Diaphragmatic or biliary visceral referral can radiate to the back or right shoulder.
Serosal inflammation causes focal abdominal tenderness.
Inflamed gallbladder under the liver produces RUQ tenderness.
Palpation during inspiration contacts an inflamed gallbladder and arrests inspiration.
Probe pressure over the inflamed gallbladder reproduces focal tenderness.
Inflamed edematous gallbladder wall thickens on US/CT/MR.
Wall edema increases measured gallbladder-wall thickness.
Acute inflammation can increase Doppler wall hyperemia.
Serosal inflammation and edema produce pericholecystic fluid.
Inflamed gallbladder irritates surrounding fat and hepatic bed.
Progressive local or diffuse inflammation causes guarding or rebound.
Inflammatory cytokines may produce fever, though fever can be absent.
Systemic inflammation raises measured temperature in many cases.
Pain, fever, hypovolemia, and sepsis can cause tachycardia.
Neutrophilic inflammation often raises WBC but can be normal in early or immunomodulated presentations.
Acute bacterial or sterile neutrophilic inflammation increases neutrophil fraction.
CRP rises with gallbladder inflammation and complicated disease.
Edema or concurrent duct stone can cause mild hyperbilirubinemia in some cholecystitis cases.
Biliary irritation or concurrent obstruction can raise alkaline phosphatase.
AST may rise with biliary obstruction, adjacent hepatic inflammation, or systemic injury.
ALT may rise with biliary obstruction or adjacent hepatic inflammation.
Common duct obstruction dilates the duct; this is a context axis for concurrent choledocholithiasis or cholangitis.
Extrahepatic obstruction raises direct bilirubin.
Gallstone passage or adjacent inflammation can produce mild to moderate lipase elevation without making pancreatitis part of the disease name.
Mural ischemia produces necrotic or gangrenous gallbladder findings.
Ongoing ischemia raises daily risk of gangrenous conversion.
Wall breach appears as discontinuity, communication, free leakage, or surgical/pathologic perforation.
Uncontrolled ischemic or necrotic wall injury increases daily perforation risk.
Contained perforation or suppuration can form pericholecystic abscess.
Hepatic-bed spread or transhepatic perforation can produce hepatic or subcapsular abscess.
Free bile leak causes chemical and infectious peritonitis.
Uncontrolled complicated gallbladder infection can progress to septic shock.
Perforation, abscess, bile peritonitis, and shock raise lifespan mortality hazard.
Successful drainage or gallbladder removal increases source-control adequacy.
After the gallbladder focus is controlled, ongoing source-control need falls.
Active antimicrobial coverage reduces susceptible bacterial burden but does not decompress an obstructed gallbladder.

Inflammatory fat stranding around the gallbladder or hepatic bed on CT/MR.

Pain localizing to the right upper quadrant.

Abdominal tenderness on examination.

Maximal tenderness when the ultrasound probe compresses the gallbladder.
Guarding, rebound, rigidity, or diffuse peritoneal irritation.

Measured body temperature.

ALT can rise with biliary obstruction or adjacent hepatic inflammation.
Lipase is usually normal in isolated cholecystitis but may be mildly or moderately elevated with gallstone passage, adjacent inflammation, or overlapping pancreatic irritation.
Common bile duct diameter; dilation supports concurrent choledocholithiasis or obstruction context.
Concurrent common-bile-duct obstruction context; relevant to ERCP and cholangitis mimic/comorbidity, not required for acute cholecystitis.

Wall discontinuity, contrast/fluid communication, free perforation, or operative/pathology evidence of perforation.

Feasibility of image-guided gallbladder drainage given anatomy, coagulopathy, interventional access, and gallbladder distension.

Clinically meaningful beta-lactam allergy context modifying antibiotic choices.
Reduced kidney function or dialysis context requiring antimicrobial and contrast dose adjustment.
Therapeutic anticoagulation, coagulopathy, or thrombocytopenia context increasing procedural bleeding risk.

Daily hazard of gallbladder perforation from necrosis, severe infection, or delayed source control.
Daily hazard of pericholecystic, hepatic-bed, or subcapsular abscess formation.
Daily hazard of free bile leak or diffuse bile peritonitis after wall breach or procedural complication.
Daily hazard of progression to septic shock physiology from uncontrolled biliary or intra-abdominal infection.

Daily death hazard emergent from age, frailty, diabetes, critical illness, pregnancy context, gangrene, perforation, abscess, bile peritonitis, septic shock, delayed source control, and treatment complications.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Stone or sludge context increases cystic duct obstruction probability.
Qualitative wall thickening and measured thickness represent the same imaging feature at different granularity.
Wall edema and pericholecystic fluid often co-occur but either can be absent.
Pericholecystic fluid and fat stranding are related expressions of local inflammation.
RUQ pain and RUQ tenderness tend to co-vary.
Both features reflect focal gallbladder tenderness, although one can be absent.
WBC and CRP are related but timing and immune modulation can decouple them.
Cholestatic context can raise bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase together.
Persistent common-duct obstruction dilates the common bile duct.
Necrotic wall is prone to perforation.
Contained wall breach can seed an abscess.
Free perforation leaks bile into the peritoneum.
Undrained abscess can progress to septic shock.
Diffuse bile/infected peritonitis raises septic shock hazard.
Shock is a major driver of death hazard.
Effective source control reduces ongoing inflammatory and septic death hazard.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Unsafe anesthesia, hostile anatomy, or absent surgical access can delay operative control.
High procedural risk can shift the source-control vector toward drainage.
Pregnancy changes positioning, imaging, anesthesia, and fetal monitoring context.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Removal of the inflamed gallbladder provides definitive source control when operative conditions permit.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Gangrenous or hostile anatomy can require a wider operative approach.
Bleeding risk may require reversal or alternate temporizing drainage.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Open operation or conversion can control severe gangrenous, perforated, or anatomically unsafe disease.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Non-distended gallbladder, unsafe access, or coagulopathy can block safe drainage.
Drainage becomes more useful when operation is unsafe or needs delay.
Drainage is only useful when the gallbladder source remains active.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Image-guided gallbladder drainage decompresses the gallbladder and temporizes source control when immediate cholecystectomy is unsafe or deferred.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Coverage must match likely or proven biliary organisms.
Severe allergy can require a different regimen.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Enteric gram-negative plus anaerobic coverage reduces bacterial and systemic inflammatory vectors while source control addresses obstruction.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Broad biliary coverage is useful when likely organisms are susceptible.
Kidney dysfunction changes exposure and toxicity risk.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Broad-spectrum beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor coverage can reduce biliary infection vectors in severe or healthcare-exposed contexts.

treatments.display_name: Carbapenem for resistant or severe context

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit depends on resistant-organism probability or susceptibility context.
Kidney dysfunction changes dosing and neurotoxicity risk.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Carbapenem coverage can reshape the bacterial vector when resistant Enterobacterales or severe sepsis context is active.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: ERCP addresses common-duct obstruction, not isolated cystic-duct obstruction.
Sphincterotomy or instrumentation bleeding risk may require mitigation.

treatments.clinical_rationale: Endoscopic duct clearance is a separate vector for concurrent choledocholithiasis or cholangitis context.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Observed stones or sludge directly raises the context axis.
Stone or sludge context increases obstruction probability.
Current pregnancy directly sets the treatment and risk context.
Pregnancy increases gallbladder stasis and sludge/stone formation.

treatment_effect_modulation.percutaneous_cholecystostomy: may gain relative utility when late gestation, multiple gestation, or operative access risk is high
treatment_effect_modulation.laparoscopic_cholecystectomy: requires pregnancy-aware anesthesia, positioning, and fetal/obstetric planning

risk_factors.display_name: Obesity, diabetes, dyslipidemia, or metabolic syndrome

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Metabolic risk increases cholesterol stone formation.

risk_factors.display_name: Older age, diabetes, or vascular disease

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Older or diabetic patients can have muted fever.
Inflammatory labs can be normal or delayed.
Microvascular disease and delayed recognition increase gangrene risk.
Comorbidity and frailty reduce reserve during sepsis or surgery.

risk_factors.display_name: Critical illness, trauma, burns, TPN, or prolonged fasting

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Acalculous presentations may lack stones while maintaining gallbladder stasis and ischemia.
Hypoperfusion and stasis increase necrosis risk.
Bedside drainage may be important when operation is unsafe.
Immune suppression can reduce fever.
Steroids and marrow state can distort WBC response.
Reduced immune containment increases severe infection risk.

risk_factors.display_name: Delayed presentation or failure to improve

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Longer untreated obstruction increases ischemia risk.
Necrosis and delayed source control increase perforation risk.
Contained complications become more likely over time.
Therapeutic anticoagulation or coagulopathy directly raises procedural bleeding context.
Bleeding risk can delay or alter procedural planning.

treatment_effect_modulation.laparoscopic_cholecystectomy: requires bleeding-risk mitigation before operation when feasible
treatment_effect_modulation.percutaneous_cholecystostomy: also requires safe access and coagulation planning

supportive_care.display_name: NPO, IV access, and procedural preparation
supportive_care.clinical_rationale: Preparation supports safe anesthesia, imaging, drainage, or operation.
Fluids support perfusion in vomiting, dehydration, sepsis, or perioperative states.
Pain control lowers distress and sympathetic activation without removing the inflammatory source.
Antiemetics and electrolyte monitoring reduce vomiting-related dehydration and perioperative risk.

supportive_care.display_name: Serial exam, labs, and imaging reassessment
supportive_care.clinical_rationale: Reassessment detects gangrene, perforation, abscess, or failed conservative response as evolving state evidence.
